summary: H.J. Res. 1 proposes an amendment to the United States Constitution to permanently set the size of the Supreme Court of the United States at nine justices, consisting of one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices.

affected_groups.effect: Its size would be permanently fixed at nine members by the Constitution.
affected_groups.group: The Supreme Court of the United States

key_provisions: Proposes a constitutional amendment to require the Supreme Court to have exactly nine justices.
Specifies that the Court must consist of one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices.
Requires ratification by the legislatures of three-fourths of the several states within seven years to become part of the Constitution.
missing_information: The text does not specify procedures for transitioning the current court if the number of justices differs at the time of ratification.
The text does not state what happens if a vacancy occurs or if justices cannot fulfill their duties.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.J. Res. 1 proposes an amendment to the United States Constitution to permanently set the size of the Supreme Court of the United States at nine justices, consisting of one Chief Justice and eight Associate Justices.
summary_detail.significance: The potential significance involves permanently anchoring the number of Supreme Court justices at nine through a constitutional amendment, preventing future changes by ordinary legislation.

title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices.
